new_findings.record: p09.move.conclude output empirical_fitness_appraisal (line 315); p09.move.ground output empirical_fitness_record
new_findings.quote: - slot: empirical_fitness_appraisal ... information_origin: [observed, derived] (conclude) vs {slot: empirical_fitness_record, type: appraisal, ... information_origin: [observed, derived, simulated]} (ground)
new_findings.criterion: P3-B-AC2 negative control (simulated or derived information must not silently become observed evidence)
new_findings.correction: The fitness appraisal comes from empirical_fitness_record through c15, and that record compares simulated model output against observed patterns. Carrying 'simulated' into the appraisal keeps that visible. Set empirical_fitness_appraisal's information_origin to [observed, derived, simulated], and make its origin_note say that the observed part is the calibration and validation targets and the simulated part is the model output they were compared with.

new_findings.criterion: P3-B-AC2 (origin-preserving handoffs; the prior finding that sensitivity variant runs need provenance)
new_findings.correction: The action that actually generates the runs receives neither parameterized_model nor variant_run_requests, so its run_receipts cannot record which parameter set or structural variant produced each run. The parent move execute does consume both, so provenance holds at Level 2; this gap is only at the execution level. Add parameterized_model (config_data) and variant_run_requests (optional_many) as inputs to p09.action.run_model, bound by retained_context edges from ground and sensitivity.

new_findings.quote: {id: p06.c36, from: p06.move.estimate, to: p06.move.refuse, ... condition: design_or_variance_cannot_be_reconstructed, from_output: error_account, to_input: error_account} ... {slot: failed_appraisal, type: appraisal, role: subject, cardinality: many, optional: false}
new_findings.criterion: P3-B-AC2 (complete records and typed topology: refusal terminals reachable with their required inputs)
new_findings.correction: The refusal route from estimate supplies only the optional error_account. The refuse record's required subject slot failed_appraisal gets nothing on this path, so the record cannot run there as written. Two fixes are possible. One: make failed_appraisal optional_many, as p07 and p09 do, and record that a variance-reconstruction failure is carried by error_account. Two: have p06.move.estimate emit an appraisal slot for design-reconstruction failure and bind it to failed_appraisal.
